field_edits.updated_text: Moderate diffuse cerebral volume loss with prominence of the cortical sulci and ventricular system, consistent with moderate cerebral atrophy. Moderate multifocal T2/FLAIR hyperintense white‑matter signal changes (leukoaraiosis), predominantly periventricular and deep, representing chronic small‑vessel ischemic gliosis. Chronic gliotic changes involving bilateral thalami consistent with old bilateral thalamic infarcts. No restricted diffusion to indicate acute infarction. No intracranial mass or hemorrhage. No midline shift or extra‑axial fluid collection. No cerebellar tonsillar ectopia. The central arterial and venous flow voids are patent.
The ventricles are enlarged consistent with moderate cerebral atrophy. The ventricular configuration otherwise is unremarkable.
Multilevel cervical spondylotic/degenerative changes with disc bulges at C2‑C3 and C3‑C4, causing mild ventral thecal sac indentation.

impression:
1. Moderate cerebral atrophy with diffuse volume loss and ventricular enlargement.
2. Moderate periventricular and deep white‑matter leukoaraiosis representing chronic small‑vessel ischemic changes.
3. Chronic bilateral thalamic lacunar infarcts.
4. Multilevel cervical spondylotic changes with disc bulges at C2‑C3 and C3‑C4 causing mild ventral thecal sac indentation.
